absent: Full memory layout and field offsets of vCPU, MMU, page fault, run and shadow page structures.
Lock ordering, interrupt context and nesting rules for MMU lock versus slot lock and invalidate lock.
Semantics of shadow synchronization, TLB flush scope, MMU generation handling and obsolete root reclamation.
Vendor exit info retrieval, hypervisor dispatch table contents and request flag lifecycle.
Complete enumeration of emulation type bits, exception vectors, debug encodings and error code bits.
Huge page level selection, private memory tests, alias detection and write tracking rules.
Instruction fetch bounds, decode cache contents and forced emulation trigger conditions.

findings.text: Address invalidation service for a vCPU scoped by a caller supplied root selector. It separates guest virtual walks from guest physical walks, suppresses noncanonical virtual invalidations, issues a virtual flush and honors a two dimensional paging shortcut, then fans out to current and retained roots only when shadow synchronization is enabled.

Shadow address synchronization is serialized with the VM wide MMU lock held exclusively across the walk of entries reachable from the supplied root. It applies only in the context of the presently installed MMU and only when the root designates a usable page, otherwise having no effect beyond clearing cached MMIO state.

Unsynchronized shadow pages encountered during address invalidation are brought up to date where possible. A synchronization failure discards the entry, and any entry that changed prompts a remote flush, while subtrees without unsynchronized descendants terminate the walk.
Event vectoring failure reporter that surfaces hypervisor exit details plus fault address and last entry CPU to userspace as an internal error with a delivery event suberror.

Emulation failure policy selects among guest exception injection and userspace reporting. VMware style faults inject a protection fault, configured exit on error or skip marked contexts report to userspace, otherwise an invalid opcode is queued with an additional userspace report when the guest is in privileged non nested state.

Emulation failure reports share a common internal error envelope carrying vendor exit reason and associated info words, an emulation suberror, and a bounded count of extra data words. Instruction bytes are optionally attached with a dedicated flag, fixed capacity padding, and size accounting.

Retry after emulation failure is permitted only for faults explicitly marked retryable and never when the fault involved a write to a shadowed page table. When permitted the referenced guest frame is unprotected and the guest is reentered, relying on separate progress guards to avoid unbounded repetition.

Software code breakpoint checks are bypassed when hardware is deemed to have already validated the instruction, including no decode, skip, trap, VMware and page fault marked emulations. Otherwise enabled breakpoints are matched against the linear instruction pointer unless inhibited.

Effective debug controls respect host debugging overrides. The effective breakpoint enable word comes from the host supplied value when hardware breakpoints are owned by the host, single step masking clears the trap flag from observed flags, and code breakpoint inhibition accounts for resume flag state and interrupt shadow behavior on Intel compatible guests.
Hardware breakpoint matching scans four debug address registers for an exact address match with compatible enable and type encoding, accumulating a bit mask of hits.

Instruction classifiers recognize a narrow set of port and counter opcodes as hypervisor backdoor operations and validate software interrupt instructions against a vector embedded in the emulation type.
Instruction decode entry initializes a fresh emulation context from current vCPU state and then decodes supplied bytes, recording emulation statistics and tracing the attempt.

Fresh emulation contexts start with no guest physical address, flags derived from current flags with single step isolated, instruction pointer from current RIP, a mode derived from protection and paging and code segment attributes, plus cleared interruptibility, exception and permission state and a reset decode cache.
Level one data cache flush requests for L1TF mitigation are expressed as a per CPU flag write that is compiled in only when CPU mitigations and Intel host support are both enabled.

Guest memory pre fault service maps a caller range using only two dimensional paging. It rejects disallowed configurations and aliased frames, reloads MMU state, distinguishes private from shared direct mappings, and reports the portion covered by the installed mapping accounting for huge page extent.

Page pre fault handling retries transient faults while honoring signals and VM death, converts fixed, spurious and write protected outcomes to success, treats emulation as missing, and treats other outcomes as input output errors with a one time warning.

Asynchronous page ready handling ignores private accesses, mismatched directness, broadcast wakeups, failed MMU reloads, and stale address spaces for indirect roots. Accepted completions reissue the fault and count only fixed outcomes.

Private page mapping requires the slot table lock held by the caller and asserts the guest memory invalidate lock for guest memory backed slots, then performs the map under shared MMU protection with retry on transient contention.

Private mapping is limited to enabled two dimensional MMU configurations, rejects write tracked frames, prepares MMU and memory caches, and succeeds only when the map operation reports a fixed result, otherwise reporting signal, dead VM, permission or input output failure.

MMU root cache reuse prefers the current root when its page, address space identifier and role match, otherwise rotates through retained roots to find a match, freeing or compacting on miss. Successful PGD switches request a PGD load, optionally request synchronization and flush on reuse, clear cached MMIO state, and reset write flooding accounting for indirect roots.
Special roots without an associated shadow page are discarded before cache lookup, limiting fast reuse to ordinary roots.
MMIO shadow entries are refreshed in place when the frame matches and cleared when the frame changed, with non MMIO entries left untouched.
Page table type selector values distinguish EPT style from sixty four bit and thirty two bit paging styles, with eighteen identifying the EPT variant.
EPT reserved bits masks are rebuilt separately for nested guest physical walks from vCPU state and for shadow contexts from host wide parameters, honoring execute only and huge page level inputs.
Synchronizing an MMU other than the currently installed one would violate walker assumptions; the implementation guards this with a one time warning and early return.
Reused previous roots can be stale with respect to MMU generation changes; obsolescence is handled by a separate free obsolete roots request rather than inline validation.
Trace helpers expose instruction emulation start and failure events as thin wrappers over a common emulation trace point with distinct outcome indicators.
Flag accessor exposes current rflags with host single step masking for use by emulation and breakpoint logic.
Asynchronous page ready callback provides the completion path for previously pending guest faults.
Private frame mapping service installs a predetermined host frame for a guest frame in guest memory backed slots.
PGD change service attempts fast reuse of cached roots for a new guest page directory base.

Root caching maintains one current root plus a small fixed set of retained roots, each described by a host page reference and for indirect roots an address space identifier, with role comparison governing reuse.
